what.text: This page follows refugees from Sri Lanka living in India, where Tamils fleeing violence crossed the Palk Strait to Tamil Nadu.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 89507 Sri Lankan refugees in India, 60.3% of all refugees from Sri Lanka.
France is the next largest host.

why.text: Anti-Tamil violence across Sri Lanka in July 1983 is widely described as the start of large-scale flight to India.
UCDP records armed conflict over Eelam territory, with the LTTE among the government's opponents, in 1984 to 2001, in 2003 and from 2005 to 2009.
The Sri Lankan army defeated the LTTE in May 2009, which UCDP records as the last year of this conflict.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 1990 at its highest point, 200000, during a second wave of arrivals from 1990 to 1994.
Former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated at Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu, by an LTTE suicide bomber on 21 May 1991.
The figure then fell, and changed only slowly and steadily from 2010 to 2019.

how.text: India has not signed the 1951 Refugee Convention, and UNHCR's total does not separate refugees in government camps from those outside them.
For 2016, the Government of India's figures are 37843 higher than UNHCR's; the sources count on different dates.
India's Citizenship (Amendment) Act, passed on 12 December 2019, does not cover Sri Lankan Tamil refugees.
